intro: The people you employ: how the organisation is divided, who works there and what is kept about them, their shifts, attendance and leave, their pay and payslips, and their reviews and goals. Every member of your organisation is staff, and each person sees their own record on their profile.
start: Make your departments, teams and jobs, so each person has a place.
Add your staff, with their department, team, job and pay group.
Set your kinds of leave, then give the year's leave to everyone.
Set up pay: a pay group, its periods, your salary components and tax tables, then each person's salary structure.
Make your shifts and a rotation plan, and fill the rota for the weeks ahead.

articles.title: Set up departments, teams and jobs
articles.summary: Divide the organisation into departments, put teams in them with a lead, and list the jobs people do.

steps.rest: on Departments. Give it a name, what it does and where it is.

steps.lead: Open Teams and press New team.
steps.rest: Choose its department and who leads it.
everyone works one shift, or people rotate between shifts. For one shift, choose its shift.
and add the jobs people do. Each list shows how many people are in it.

tips: A team's lead is the manager who decides that team's leave and rates their reviews.

articles.title: Add a new member of staff
articles.summary: Add someone with their work email, where they work and the day they start. The rest of their record can come later.

steps.rest: on Staff.

steps.lead: Enter their name and work email.
steps.rest: Their work email is how they are told things.

steps.lead: Choose their department, team and job,
steps.rest: and give their staff number, the date hired and their first day of work. Pay counts from the first day.

articles.title: Record that someone is leaving
articles.summary: Give their last day and why. Until that day they show as working their notice; after it, as left.

steps.rest: from Staff.
Give their last day, why they are leaving, and a note if you want.
They show as working their notice until the last day, then as left. Their record is kept.

tips: Recorded by mistake? Press Reinstate on their page.
Payroll stops paying someone once they have left before a period begins.

articles.title: Answer a request to change someone's details
articles.summary: When someone suggests a change to their own record, HR sees what it says now and what they ask for, and approves or refuses it.

steps.rest: What is waiting for HR is on the first tab.
on the request. You see what it says now, what they ask for and what they said.
When you refuse, write why, so they know. The request moves to its tab.

tips: People ask from their own profile: My details › Suggest a change.

articles.title: Keep certificates and checks in date
articles.summary: See whose licences, training, checks and medicals have expired or expire within 30 days, and renew them in place.

steps.rest: It opens on what has expired or expires within 30 days, soonest first.
to add a record: the person, the kind, what it is, its number, when it was issued and when it expires, with a copy.
when the new one comes in: give its new expiry and upload the new copy.

articles.title: Set up shifts and fill the rota
articles.summary: Make your shifts, put them in a rotation plan for a team, and fill the rota for the weeks ahead in one go.
before: Make each shift on Shifts with New shift: its hours, break, the people needed and its team.

steps.rest: on Rotation plans and choose the team.
and the working days.

steps.lead: Choose how often people move on
steps.rest: (every day, week or month) and the grace for clocking in.
with the days from and to. Holidays and approved leave are left out, and anyone already on the rota stays as they are.

tips: Fill the rota twice and it adds nothing new.
To change one day, open Rota, press Put them on the shift, or Take off on a place.

articles.title: See who came in today, and who is late
articles.summary: Everyone on the rota for a day, when they clocked in and out, who is late and who is not in.

steps.rest: and choose the day and team.

steps.rest: on someone's row to record it for them.

tips: Clocking in after the shift's grace is late; clocking out before its end is leaving early.
Whether people clock themselves in, and whether no clock-in becomes absent, are set in Document settings › Attendance and rotas.

articles.title: Add a public holiday
articles.summary: Holidays are kept per place, and are left out of the rota and of leave counts.

steps.rest: on Holidays.
and where it is kept, or the whole organisation.
It shows under Coming up, and leave asked for that day does not count it.

articles.title: Set up leave and give everyone this year's days
articles.summary: Make each kind of leave with its days a year and carry-over, then give the year's leave to everyone in one step.

steps.rest: on Kinds of leave.

steps.lead: Give its name and days a year,
steps.rest: whether it is paid, and the most carried into the next year (or nothing).
choose the year and press Give the year's leave to everyone. Each person gets each kind's days, plus what they carry over.
Each person has the days given, carried over, taken, waiting and what they can still ask for.

tips: Giving the year's leave twice adds nothing: only people with no entitlement yet get one.
Leave that has begun is corrected by changing the entitlement, not by cancelling it.

articles.title: Approve or refuse a leave request
articles.summary: See the person's balance, the notice they gave and who else is away, then decide.

steps.rest: Waiting for a decision is the first tab.
on a request. The side panel shows the balance now and after this, the notice given, and the cover on the rota for each day.
and approve or refuse it there, saying why when you refuse.

articles.after: Approved, the days come off the balance and the person is left off the rota. Refused, nothing is taken.
tips: People ask from their own profile: My leave › Ask for leave. To record leave for someone, press Ask for leave on someone's behalf.
Cancelling an approved leave that has not begun gives the days back.

articles.title: Set up payroll
articles.summary: A pay group, its periods, your salary components and the tax table, so a run can work out everyone's pay.

steps.rest: on Pay groups: its name, currency, how often it is paid, the country taxed in, and a minimum net if you want one.
and press Make the periods for the group's year.
and add each part of pay, such as housing or pension: its kind, whether it is part of gross pay, taxed or taken before tax.
and press New tax table: the country, residents or non-residents, from when, and a flat rate or brackets.

tips: A component paid by the employer, on top of pay, is never in the person's gross, tax or net, but reaches the books.
Name who a component or tax table is paid over to, so a paid run can pay it on.

articles.title: Set or raise someone's salary
articles.summary: Give a person a base salary and the components added or taken each period, from a date.

steps.rest: It shows each person's pay group and salary today, and who is not set to be paid.

articles.title: Run payroll and pay everyone
articles.summary: Make a run for a pay group's period, calculate it, check each person, approve it and pay it. Paying posts to the books and makes the payslips.

steps.rest: on Payroll runs, and choose the pay group, the period and the pay date.

Anyone paid below the group's minimum net is marked. Change what is wrong and press Calculate again.
It is ready to pay.

It is posted to the books and a payslip is made for each person.

tips: To send net pay to each person through Finance, use Ask to pay in the run's Payment section. Each person needs an approved account in Beneficiaries.
People find their payslips on their own profile, under My payslips.

articles.title: Void a payroll run
articles.summary: Reverse a run in the books and say how the money comes back. The run and its payslips are kept, marked void.
before: Cancel any payment request made from the run, or get a paid one back first.

steps.rest: and press Void.

steps.lead: Say how the money comes back:
steps.rest: it was returned to the bank (and the account it came back into), or recover it from the employees.
The run is reversed in the books and kept, marked void.

articles.title: Run a review cycle
articles.summary: Make a cycle with its dates, launch it so everyone gets a review, and close it once every review is finalised.
before: List the competencies people are rated on in Competencies, each with its weight.

steps.rest: on Review cycles: its name, the period, and when self-assessments and managers' ratings are due.

steps.lead: Open the cycle and press Launch the cycle.
steps.rest: Everyone in it gets a review, rated by their team's lead, with the competencies in use and their goals.
on the cycle's page. Press Review the newcomers for anyone who joined since.
once every review is finalised. It can be reopened.

articles.title: Rate someone's performance review
articles.summary: The person rates themselves first; their manager then rates each line, writes a summary and finalises it.

steps.rest: Once the person has submitted, you see their own rating and summary.
A low rating needs a reason.
then press Finalise. It is scored and shown to the person.

articles.after: The person reads it and acknowledges it, with a comment.
tips: HR can change who rates a review, and reopen a finalised one. Its scores are cleared and it goes back to its manager.

articles.title: Set goals and follow their progress
articles.summary: Give someone goals for the cycle, break them into tasks with boxes to tick, and watch progress move on the board.

steps.rest: and press New goal on its board. Choose whose goal it is, how it is measured and its weight.
and add its tasks, each with boxes to tick.

steps.lead: Tick boxes as work is done.
steps.rest: The task's progress follows, and the goal's follows its tasks.

tips: Goals lists every goal across cycles, with whose it is and its progress.
